9	/-!
10	# The datum-level Abel–Jacobi map and its pointing law (Wave 6, `ofCurve`/`comp_ofCurve`)
11	
12	`Picard/AbelElement.lean` builds the Abel element `abelElement C P : pic0Subgroup C C` and
13	proves the pointing law `abelElement_map_point`.  `Picard/JacobianData.lean` pins the
14	representability datum with its universal property `homEquiv : (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T`.
15	This file is the one-line bridge between them that the frozen Wave-6 gates consume:
16	
17	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofCurve` — the Abel–Jacobi map `C ⟶ d.J` of a rational
18	  point, `d.homEquiv.symm (abelElement C P)`.  The frozen `Jacobian.ofCurve`
19	  (`Challenge.lean:125`) is `(jacobianData C).ofCurve P` on the nose, since
20	  `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`.
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.homEquiv_one` — the universal property sends the unit
22	  section to the trivial class.  This is *not* free: `η[d.J]` is `MonObj.one` of
23	  `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`, which mathlib defines as `α.homEquiv'.symm 1`; the content
24	  is that `RepresentableBy.homEquiv'` (`ConcreteCategory/Representable.lean`) is
25	  `homEquiv` itself, so the two cancel.
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.comp_ofCurve` — **the pointing law**
27	  `P ≫ d.ofCurve P = η[d.J]`, the datum-level avatar of the frozen
28	  `Jacobian.comp_ofCurve` (`Challenge.lean:130`).  Proved by injectivity of `homEquiv`,
29	  its naturality `homEquiv_comp` against `pic0Map`, and `abelElement_map_point`.
30	
31	Nothing here assumes a producer for `jacobianData`; everything is stated for an arbitrary
32	`d : JacobianData C`, in the section-variable discipline `JacobianData.lean` fixes.  The
33	universal-property half of Wave 6 (`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`, `Challenge.lean:141`) is
34	NOT addressed here and has no avatar anywhere.
35	-/
36	
37	set_option autoImplicit false
38	
39	universe u
40	
41	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
42	
43	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
44	
45	namespace JacobianData
46	
47	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
48	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
49	
50	/-- **The datum-level Abel–Jacobi map** (design §4.6; the frozen `Jacobian.ofCurve`,
51	`Challenge.lean:125`): the morphism `C ⟶ d.J` classifying the Abel element of the
52	rational point `P`.  Already used unnamed at
53	`Picard/JacobianDataBaseChangeAbel.lean:115`; naming it is what makes the frozen gate a
54	one-liner. -/
55	noncomputable def ofCurve (d : JacobianData C) (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
56	    C ⟶ d.J :=
57	  d.homEquiv.symm (abelElement C P)
58	
59	@[simp]
60	theorem homEquiv_ofCurve (d : JacobianData C) (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
61	    d.homEquiv (d.ofCurve P) = abelElement C P :=
62	  d.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply _
63	
64	/-- **The universal property sends the unit section to the trivial class**: the group
65	structure `d.grpObj` is `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`, whose `one` is by definition
66	`d.rep.homEquiv'.symm 1`, and `RepresentableBy.homEquiv'` IS `homEquiv` — so the two
67	cancel by `Equiv.apply_symm_apply`. -/
68	theorem homEquiv_one (d : JacobianData C) :
69	    letI := d.grpObj
70	    d.homEquiv (η[d.J]) = 1 :=
71	  d.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply 1
72	
73	/-- **The pointing law** (the frozen `Jacobian.comp_ofCurve`, `Challenge.lean:130`): the
74	Abel–Jacobi map of `P` sends `P` itself to the neutral element of the group scheme
75	`d.J`.  Injectivity of the universal property reduces it to the naturality square
76	`homEquiv (P ≫ f) = pic0Map C P (homEquiv f)` and the landed pointing law
77	`abelElement_map_point`. -/
78	theorem comp_ofCurve (d : JacobianData C) (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
79	    letI := d.grpObj
80	    P ≫ d.ofCurve P = η[d.J] := by
81	  letI := d.grpObj
82	  refine d.homEquiv.injective ?_
83	  rw [d.homEquiv_comp P (d.ofCurve P), homEquiv_ofCurve, homEquiv_one]
84	  exact abelElement_map_point P
85	
86	end JacobianData
87	
88	end AlgebraicGeometry

11	
12	`DivRepAffinePullback` (`Picard/DivRepAffKit.lean`) is the exact output F5 owes before the
13	affine representability equivalence is packaged.  As landed it demands FOUR fields:
14	`pull`, `pull_classify`, `isDivRepClassify_pull` and `pull_naturality`.
15	
16	The separation theorem (`Picard/DivRepClassifyZarSep.lean`) makes `pull_classify`
17	**redundant**: if the pulled class of every morphism satisfies the characterizing clause
18	for that morphism, then in particular `pull (classify F)` and `F` are both classified by
19	`classify F`, so they are equal.  This file records that.
20	
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pull_classify_of_isDivRepClassify_pull` — the reduction, stated for a
22	  bare `pull` function so it can be used before any package exists.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.ofPull` — **the three-field constructor**.  A
24	  producer now owes `pull`, the clause law, and naturality; the round-trip law is derived.
25	
26	This does not produce a `DivRepAffinePullback` — there is still no producer of one — but
27	it removes one of the four obligations from whoever writes it, and it is the obligation
28	that would otherwise have to be re-proved by a second cover chase.
29	-/

88	    (hpull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),
89	      IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (pull S v) v.left)
90	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (F : DivFamZar C S pi g) :
91	    pull S (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F) = F :=
92	  eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 _ F
93	    (hpull S (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F))
94	    (divRepClassifyZar_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F)

100	derived from `isDivRepClassify_pull` by `pull_classify_of_isDivRepClassify_pull`, so a
101	producer owes only the pullback map, the characterizing clause it satisfies, and
102	naturality. -/

104	    (pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S],
105	      (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) → DivFamZar C S pi g)
106	    (hpull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),

114	    pull hpull
115	  isDivRepClassify_pull := hpull
116	  pull_naturality := hnat

123	    (hpull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),

125	    (hnat : ∀ {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]

127	      pull B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v) = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (pull A v))

structure DivRepAffinePullback where

    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) → DivFamZar C S pi g
  pull_classify : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (F : DivFamZar C S pi g),
    pull S (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F) = F

    (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),
    IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (pull S v) v.left
  pull_naturality : ∀ {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B) (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver),

/-- The affine representability equivalence assembled from an F5 pullback package.
The inverse is the landed backward classifier; its hom-side inverse law follows from
`divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify`. -/
noncomputable def equiv
    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] :
    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) ≃ DivFamZar C S pi g where
  toFun := D.pull S
  invFun := divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S
  left_inv v :=
    (divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
      (D.pull S v) v (D.isDivRepClassify_pull S v)).symm
  right_inv := D.pull_classify S

theorem equiv_apply
    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) :
    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S v = D.pull S v :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem equiv_symm_apply
    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (F : DivFamZar C S pi g) :
    (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
      (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S).symm F
      = divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F :=
  rfl

    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B)
    (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver) :

        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v)

The affine-level heart of the shared CHART-U(b) brick, stated directly on a pinned
basic-open cocycle datum in the **witness form** the `chartLocus` predicate uses.

For a datum `D` over an affine base `B`, the locus of primes `q` of `B` at which the

campaign (`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing`, Noetherian-free — dat-d §3.5) read

(`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness`,

condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗[B] κ(q))`, and the dictionary rewrites it,
pointwise and class-intrinsically, as the effective-witness/h¹-vanishing condition.

**(b) ADDENDUM 2 §4's "tractable half" is not a half, and its argument is circular.**
Θ = `fiberWeilDivisor π` is supported on `V₀ ∖ V₁` (`RiemannRoch/FLVFiberToolkit.lean:292`,

its piece, so `supportLocus` is the base locus of `K`, and "a generator of exact pole order `a`
exists at `y ∈ Θ`" holds iff the base locus misses `y`. Premise = conclusion.

**(c) There is an explicit counterexample, and no Zariski shrink of the base evades it.**
Over `k[t]`, on `C = P¹`, `π = id`, take the degree-2 form

  `F = t·X² + X·Y + t·Y²`,   `D = Z(F) ⊆ P¹ × A¹_t`.

divisor, finite flat of degree 2. `F(1,0) = F(0,1) = t`, so the fibre `D₀ = Z(XY) = {0, ∞}`

coprime coefficients, hence irreducible in `k[x,t]`; the only point over `Y = 0` is `(∞, 0)`,
which lies in the closure (`t = -x/(x²+1) → 0` as `x → ∞`). So `D` is IRREDUCIBLE. `D → A¹_t`

witness. The conclusion stands; the witness above is the correct one.

(`Picard/DivSchemeCertZarConfine.lean`) — the support locus is a `DivEq` invariant, because the

escape hatch. `DivFamZar` is not the relative-divisor functor, and `divRep` stated against it
represents the wrong object.

`FinCoverData` (`Picard/DivisorFamily.lean:160-176`) hardwires `h₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(V₀)`,

* refining the cover cannot help (more pieces, same union of traces);

**R2 — generalize `FinCoverData` to σ-charts.** For `σ ∈ H⁰(bΘ)` let `U_σ` be its
non-vanishing locus; `V₀` and `V₁` are the cases `σ = t₀ᵇ`, `t₁ᵇ`. A divisor avoiding `Z(σ)` is
swallowed by the single piece `U_σ`. This stays inside the existing `relThetaSections`
vocabulary, but owes affineness of `U_σ` (complement of an ample divisor) and a wide refactor
of `FinCoverData`/`DivisorAdaptation`/`chartProd`.

(colength j)` is free from fibrewise regularity alone
(`flat_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField`, `SupportTube.lean:313` — no finiteness, no
no-leak), while `Module.Finite` is exactly the culprit. But the (c2)/(c3)/(c4) keystones
(`SlicingFlatKernel.lean`, variable block at :221-224) all carry `[Module.Finite R M]` with
`M = chartProd`, which IS finite colengths. Dropping (c1) leaves `projective_glued`,
`rankAtStalk_glued` and both flat-cokernel clauses with no landed route. Do not re-propose this

### 4. Why a repair of this shape is legitimate at all

§Discipline (2) forbids a support-separation hypothesis, and it is right to: assuming
`supp D ∩ π⁻¹({0,∞}) = ∅` about an arbitrary divisor assumes the conclusion. The repair does
something different — the ATLAS RECORDS which vertical fibres its divisors avoid — and that is
legitimate because the recorded condition is **open on the base**. New this round,

* `isOpen_setOf_fibre_subset_chartInter` — the base points whose support fibre lies in

* `exists_opens_supportLocus_subset_chartInter` — confinement at one fibre spreads to a

* `supportLocus_subset_of_forall_fibre` — fibrewise confinement at every base point IS the

owes is that the carved opens **cover** — and with the two pinned charts fixed once and for all

/-- The exact output expected from F5 before the affine equivalence is packaged.
`isDivRepClassify_pull` is the hom-side law in the refinement-stable clause spelling;
classifier uniqueness turns it into the second inverse law automatically. -/
structure DivRepAffinePullback where
  pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S],
    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) → DivFamZar C S pi g
  pull_classify : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (F : DivFamZar C S pi g),
    pull S (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F) = F
  isDivRepClassify_pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),
    IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (pull S v) v.left
  pull_naturality : ∀ {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B) (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver),
    pull B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v) = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (pull A v)

namespace DivRepAffinePullback

/-- The affine representability equivalence assembled from an F5 pullback package.
The inverse is the landed backward classifier; its hom-side inverse law follows from
`divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify`. -/
noncomputable def equiv
    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] :
    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) ≃ DivFamZar C S pi g where
  toFun := D.pull S
  invFun := divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S
  left_inv v :=
    (divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
      (D.pull S v) v (D.isDivRepClassify_pull S v)).symm
  right_inv := D.pull_classify S

@[simp]
theorem equiv_apply
    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) :
    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S v = D.pull S v :=
  rfl

theorem equiv_symm_apply
    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (F : DivFamZar C S pi g) :
    (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
      (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S).symm F

    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B)
    (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver) :
    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v)

            (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D A v) :=
